Marissa / Rishi —

Initial draft answers below. I also exported our current subprocessor registry and redacted customer IDs — attaching as redwood_subprocessors_20260905.pdf. Please review for legal phrasing and anything to redact further.

1) Subprocessors that may see plaintext request/response content (examples):
- AWS (S3 for model artifacts and EBS for ephemeral runtime disks) — plaintext only if customer uploads data to S3; for hosted API we do not retain long-term plaintext by default.
- GCP (for certain private deployments / marketplace images) — depends on customer region and deployment choice.
- Model runtime workers (managed by Redwood) — can access request/response in memory during inference; we treat these as internal subprocessors.

2) Telemetry & logging vendors (metrics only — no plaintext payloads):
- Datadog (metrics/traces) — we send metrics and sampled traces with anonymized request IDs; by default we strip full response payloads.
- Sentry (errors) — stack traces and error context; we scrub request bodies unless explicitly enabled by customer.
- Segment / Snowplow (event telemetry for product analytics) — product-level events only, no request/response payloads.

3) PII in logs:
- Default behavior: we do not log full request/response payloads long-term. Short-lived in-memory buffers exist for inference and are purged. Customer may opt-in to request logging for debugging; in that case we recommend a scoped retention policy and masking.

4) Retention defaults and controls:
- Request/response payloads: default retention = 0 days for hosted API (ephemeral), can be configured to 7/30/90 days with contractual agreement.
- Telemetry metrics/aggregates: retained 90 days by default; can be adjusted with paid plan.

5) Data residency / region pinning:
- Hosted API: routed to nearest region by default (US/EU/APAC).
- Dedicated & Private: we support EU-only Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) installs to meet EU residency.

Notes:
- Marketplace flows: when customers deploy via a cloud marketplace (AWS Marketplace, GCP Marketplace), some limited metadata related to subscription and billing flows may be exchanged with the cloud provider. We treat the cloud provider as a subprocessor for billing/marketplace purposes and document the minimal attributes shared.

Please check the attached PDF for the full redacted registry and let me know edits. I can tighten wording on any of these points for procurement.

Hi Tom / Security team —

Thanks for the patience. Please find attached our redacted subprocessor registry and a short answersheet to the items you flagged. Highlights below:

- Plaintext access: internal runtime workers and our managed storage (AWS/GCP per-deployment) may transiently access plaintext during inference. By default we do not retain plaintext tokens long-term for hosted API.
- Telemetry: Datadog and Sentry receive metrics/errors with anonymized request IDs. We do not send full response bodies to telemetry vendors by default; customers may enable request logging in limited contexts.
- Retention defaults: hosted API ephemeral (0 days); configurable to 7/30/90 days via contract.
- Data residency: we support EU-only Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments for customers who require EU-only processing.
- Marketplace flows: when deployed via cloud marketplaces, minimal billing/subscription metadata is shared with the cloud provider. We document this in the registry.

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_20260905.pdf (redacted for external sharing)
